text:
maria: Anyone repro a goroutine leak when cancelling generator-style streams in the Go SDK? I hooked our sampleapp and after a few cancels the process goroutine count climbs.
jin: yep, saw something like that last week. seemed tied to auth retry path holding a channel open.
alice: do you have a minimal trace or stack? quick clues are helpful.
maria: minimal repro attached in the sampleapp. gist link: https://gist.github.com/redwood/repro1
maria: stack snippet pasted below:
```
runtime: goroutine stack dump:
1 @ 0x... runtime.newproc
1 @ 0x... net/http.(*persistConn).readLoop
1 @ 0x... github.com/redwoodinc/go-sdk/gen.(*streamConn).recvLoop
1 @ 0x... github.com/redwoodinc/go-sdk/internal/auth.(*tokenRefresher).watch
```
samir: sounds like token refresher goroutine isn't returning when the stream ctx is cancelled.
jin: exact. in our code the refresher waits on a done channel that only closes on full connection teardown, not per-request ctx cancel.
alice: is the refresher per-connection or shared across multiple streams? if shared, cancellation semantics are tricky.
maria: it's per-connection right now, but our generator API spins a new connection per stream. if cancel leaves connection in limbo (auth retry loop), goroutine stays.
jin: workaround: explicitly call client.Close() on cancel in the sampleapp; that forces teardown.
alice: works, but onboarding docs don't mention this. new users will think ctx cancel is enough.
maria: agreed — big DX friction. people expect ctx cancellation to free all resources.
samir: two actionable items:
- make token refresher observe the request ctx in addition to connection lifecycle
- document the current behavior in the sample app and README (or better, change before next release)
jin: code suggestion — pass a ctx into startRefresher(ctx context.Context, ...). inside select: case <-ctx.Done(): return
alice: small patch I sketched:
```
func startRefresher(parent context.Context, ...) {
    ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(parent)
    go func() {
        defer cancel()
        for {
            select {
            case <-ctx.Done():
                return
            case <-time.After(refreshInterval):
                // refresh logic
            }
        }
    }()
}
```
maria: that looks good. also we should avoid subtle global state; prefer per-stream contexts that close on cancel.
dev-bot: deploy-checklist: add unit test for stream cancel + token refresh, update onboarding sample app docs.
samir: another ergonomic idea: make the generator API return a helper that exposes Close() and Done() so user doesn't have to remember client.Close(). example: g, err := client.NewGenerator(ctx, ...); defer g.Close()
jin: yes, returning a stream object with explicit lifecycle methods is more idiomatic in Go.
alice: also call out in docs how auth retry/backoff behaves during active streams (we should surface whether retries are per-connection or per-request).
maria: I'll file a GH issue with repro + stack and link the PR for the patch sketch. thanks for the quick checks :pray:
samir: ping @eng-runtime if anyone wants to pair on the refresher change.
jin: putting a small unit test on my queue.
maria: thanks all :thumbsup:
